document.title: Add refresh: carry a review over to new commits without starting over
document.summary: A new `refresh` command re-points an existing `review.json` to the commits its refs resolve to now, and the skill gains a Refresh branch that rewrites only the groups the report names. `pregroup` and `review` record the resolved commits in `source` so `refresh` knows where the last review stood.
document.why: [#88](source:s1) says hosted reviews go stale after a rebase or new commits, and agents re-index, rewrite `review.json`, export, and republish by hand. The [session](source:s4) asked for incremental updates that are efficient and that avoid a skill redesign where possible.

sources.title: Refresh hosted PR reviews after rebase (and pin base/head SHAs)
sources.gist: Asks for a one-shot refresh path after a rebase, recorded base and head SHAs with a warning on mismatch, and optionally a command tied to a PR number.

sources.label: PR #146
sources.title: Add refresh: carry a review over to new commits without starting over
sources.gist: Closes #88 with a refresh command, pinned commits in source, and a Refresh branch in the skill.

sources.label: Add refresh: carry a review over to new commits without starting over
sources.gist: Names the hunk matching rules: same changed lines keep the ref, an edit in the same region is changed, the rest is new or gone.

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 21
sources.gist: Máté asked for incremental updates to a PR review without regenerating it, done efficiently, and preferred no full skill redesign.

lookFor: [#88](source:s1) asks to display the recorded SHAs and to fail or warn when the work tree does not match. Done differently: `serve` and `export` print a note to stderr naming `refresh` when the refs resolve elsewhere; the UI still shows the live resolved SHAs and nothing fails. `validate` prints no such note.
[#88](source:s1) suggests a command tied to a PR number. Not done: the skill reads the previous document from a hosted export's `api/review.json` with `curl` and `jq`, and the CLI stays forge-free.

[#88](source:s1) wants a one-shot path. Done differently: the skill's Refresh branch is five steps (refresh and cat, sources, show, edit, validate and export). The CLI does the mechanical part in one command; the prose still needs the agent.
No eval case runs `refresh`; coverage is the unit and integration tests in `src/review/refresh.test.ts`. The eval harness has no shape for a previous document plus a later head.

groups.title: Record the resolved commits in source
groups.why: [#88](source:s1) asks to record the base and head SHAs. `refresh` needs them to know which range the document was written for; a branch ref alone resolves to the new head and hides the old one.
groups.summary: `resolveSource` in `src/git/diff.ts` puts `baseSha` and `headSha` into `source`, and `src/schema/review.ts` accepts them as optional fields.
lookFor: Both fields are optional, so a document written by an older CLI still parses, serves, and validates. Only `refresh` rejects it, with a message that names `pregroup`.

groups.title: Match hunks across ranges and rewrite the refs
groups.why: The [commit](source:s3) names the rules: a hunk with the same path and changed lines keeps its ref, an edit in the same region is changed and keeps its group, everything else is new or gone. This group is that engine and its report.
groups.summary: `matchHunks` in `src/review/refresh.ts` pairs old and new hunks as same, changed, or reformat, `refreshDocument` re-points or drops refs and drafts an `update` group for uncovered hunks, `formatRefresh` prints the delta digest, `listNewSubjects` in `src/git/log.ts` lists the new commit subjects, and `reviewFileBody` moves from the test helper into `src/review/write.ts`.
lookFor: Subtle. An edited hunk pairs with the first unmatched old hunk in the same file whose old-side line range overlaps, context lines included. One old hunk split into two reports the second as new; two old hunks merged into one report the second old as gone. Both cases are honest, just noisier than the common edit.
Image hunks have no lines, so they match on the file's `headerPatch` (the blob ids). A changed image is reported as changed, not same.
A located ref that matched neither the previous diff nor the live diff is dropped and counted as gone. Nothing is invented in its place.

`listNewSubjects` runs `git log --right-only --cherry-pick old...new ^base`, so a rebase lists only the commits added on top and a merge of the base lists the merge commit plus new work. Upstream commits never appear.
`refreshDocument` returns a new document; the input is not mutated. The written key order follows the schema, so a refreshed file may reorder top-level keys once.

A changed hunk whose added text and removed text are the same once every whitespace character is dropped is `reformat`, not `changed`. Both small-delta simulation runs spent their one `show` fetch on such a hunk; the skill now skips that fetch.

groups.title: The refresh command and the drift note
groups.why: [#88](source:s1) asks for a refresh path and a warning when the review no longer matches the commits. This group wires both into the CLI.
groups.summary: `cmdRefresh` in `src/cli/commands.ts` loads the document, resolves the refs again, diffs both ranges, writes the result, and returns the report; `sourceDrift` builds the note that `serve` and `export` print in `src/cli/main.ts`; `src/cli/args.ts` adds the command and its usage text. Two fixes from the simulation runs ride along: `cmdShow` keeps the old path of a renamed hunk ref, and `cmdPregroup` leaves lockfiles out of the draft.
lookFor: `refresh` writes `review.json` before it prints the report. A run that finds both commits unchanged prints `nothing to refresh` and does not touch the file.

The old range is read from `source.baseSha` and `source.headSha`; the new refs default to `source.baseRef` and `source.headRef`, so a document written for `origin/main...origin/feature` refreshes with no flags after `git fetch`.
The drift note goes to stderr on `serve` and `export` only. `validate` stays silent about it.

`show --hunk "old -> new@a+b"` used to print `no hunk matches` because `readPathDiff` got only the new path and git saw an added file. It now passes the old path too, so the ref `pregroup` and `refresh` write is the ref `show` reads.
`pregroup` skipped lockfiles in the skeleton but still listed them in the draft groups through the digest. They are now skipped there as well, which matches the skill text.
The hint after `refresh` says `Check the prose of the groups named above`, not `Rewrite`, because a group whose hunks only reformatted keeps its prose.

groups.title: The Refresh branch in the skill
groups.why: The [session](source:s4) asked for the skill to support incremental updates. The new section tells the agent to copy the previous document, run `refresh`, fetch only new sources and new or changed hunks, and edit the named groups in place.
groups.summary: `skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md` gains a Refresh section, a trigger in the description, a pointer at the top of the Workflow, and a stale-ref bullet that names `refresh`; `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md` is the identical synced copy and `src/schema/skill-sync.test.ts` pins the new sentence. After the simulation runs the `show` examples carry `--base` and `--head`, the refresh fetch budget counts the files the report lists, `same` and `reformat` hunks are fetched only when a kept bullet rests on them, and a named group whose hunks keep their meaning keeps its prose.
lookFor: The `.agents` copy is identical to `skills-next`; read one. `pnpm check:skill` passes.
Step 4 tells the agent to edit `review.json` in place instead of the one full write the main Workflow uses. That is the efficiency lever: unchanged groups never leave the file.

Every simulated agent added `--base` and `--head` to `show` on its own, or lost a call to the default range. The Workflow step-5 example now carries both flags; that change touches the main flow, not only Refresh.

groups.title: README and glossary
groups.why: The CLI gains a command and `source` gains fields, so the user-facing docs name them.
groups.summary: `README.md` adds `comprehende refresh` to the CLI section and `docs/glossary.md` defines Refresh and lists the full command set.

groups.title: Regenerated JSON Schema copies
groups.why: `pnpm generate:schema` and `pnpm sync:skill` regenerate the JSON Schema from `src/schema/review.ts`; the three copies are identical output.
groups.summary: Each copy adds the two optional `baseSha` and `headSha` properties under `source`. Skip them; the Zod schema in the first group is the source.

commits.subject: Refresh: tell a reformat apart from an edit
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A changed hunk whose added and removed text is the same once whitespace is dropped is reported as reformat. Both small-delta simulation runs spent their one show fetch learning that, so the skill now skips the fetch for a reformat hunk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Refresh: fix show on renamed hunk refs, keep prose when a named group only reformats
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Add refresh: carry a review over to new commits without starting over
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
pregroup and review record the commits the refs resolved to in source.baseSha and source.headSha. refresh resolves the refs again and diffs the old range against the new one per hunk: a hunk with the same path and changed lines keeps its ref (re-pointed when only the start moved), a hunk edited in the same region is changed and keeps its group, a ref whose hunk left the diff is dropped, and hunks no group covers land in a draft update group. It prints the new commit subjects and one line per changed file so the skill rewrites only what changed. serve and export note when the refs drifted from the recorded commits.

The skill gains a Refresh branch that reuses the sources, validate and serve steps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
